title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 8 Introduction to Trigonometry (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
short_title: Class 10 Maths · Ch 8 Introduction to Trigonometry
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. No calculator.

S1.name: The six ratios and their limits
S1.tip: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj; cosec, sec, cot are reciprocals. For an acute angle sin and cos are below 1; sec and cosec are at least 1.

S2.name: One ratio given: find the rest
S2.tip: Draw the triangle, write the known sides as multiples of k, find the third by Pythagoras. For an expression in sin and cos with tan given, divide top and bottom by cos A.

S3.name: Standard angles table
S3.tip: sin: 0, 1/2, 1/√2, √3/2, 1 (0° to 90°); cos is the same list backwards; tan: 0, 1/√3, 1, √3, not defined.

S4.name: Evaluate expressions
S4.tip: Substitute, then square: sin²60° = (sin 60°)² = 3/4. Simplify fractions last.

S5.name: Find the angles
S5.tip: Turn each value into an angle, then add and subtract: A − B = 30°, A + B = 60° → A = 45°, B = 15°.

S6.name: The three identities
S6.tip: sin²A + cos²A = 1, 1 + tan²A = sec²A, 1 + cot²A = cosec²A. (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1.

S7.name: Use identities to find values
S7.tip: From one ratio get the squares (tan θ = 1/√5 → sec²θ = 6/5). Square a sum: (tan A + cot A)² = tan²A + cot²A + 2.

S8.name: Proving identities
S8.tip: Start from the harder side, write everything in sin and cos, rationalise roots, aim for the other side.

S9.name: Substitution and spot-the-error
S9.tip: Square and add when two relations are given; (1 − sin θ)² = 1 − 2 sin θ + sin²θ, not cos²θ.

questions.question: If sec θ + tan θ = 3 (θ acute), find the value of 10 sin θ.
questions.explanation: (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1 → sec θ − tan θ = 1/3. Adding: sec θ = 5/3; subtracting: tan θ = 4/3. sin θ = tan θ/sec θ = 4/5 → 10 sin θ = 8 (a 2026 board type).
